A.summary:
This change adds a table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that records which
MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches, and where each name came
from. Bugs already record this to decide who may read their transcripts.
Patchsets only had mailing list labels from To:/Cc: headers, which anyone
can set, so those cannot confer authority.

The table mirrors bug_subsystems, including the source column, so that
only rows with source maintainers_section grant authority. Migration 009
creates it with a cascading foreign key to patchsets, a CHECK constraint
on source, a default of caller_supplied (the least privileged value), and
two indexes. The schema version moves from 8 to 9.

In src/db.rs there are four new methods:

add_patchset_maintainer_sections: unions sections in as each part of a
series arrives.

replace_patchset_maintainer_sections: sets the exact list and prunes stale
rows, for backfill.

authorizing_sections_for_patchset: returns only maintainers_section rows.
An empty result means nobody is authorized.

patchset_maintainer_sections: returns all rows with provenance, for
display only.

Five tests cover the union across parts, authority limited to
maintainers_section rows, the empty case, replace with pruning and
re-attribution, and isolation between patchsets.

Nothing reads these rows yet, so the only visible effect is the schema
version bump and a new empty table after migration.

Before:
  Database schema version 8; no patchset_maintainer_sections table.

After:
  Database schema version 9; an empty patchset_maintainer_sections table
  exists, and nothing queries it yet.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, used by
  Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the upsert ends in DO UPDATE
  SET source = excluded.source with no precedence rule. The add path is
  documented as a union that never narrows, but a later series part that
  supplies a name already stored as maintainers_section with a weaker source
  (path_prefix or caller_supplied) silently demotes it.
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset filters on maintainers_section, so the
  section stops authorizing and its maintainers lose transcript access.
  Part arrival order decides the result. The new tests use net as both a
  path prefix and a MAINTAINERS name, so a collision is plausible.
  test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts only re-adds a name with the same
  source, so it cannot catch this. The failure is closed and latent since
  nothing reads the rows yet. Fix: on the add path keep the stronger source,
  for example CASE WHEN excluded.source = 'maintainers_section' THEN
  excluded.source ELSE source END, and add a test with conflicting sources.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (patchset merge transaction) and
  src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql, the new table has
  ON DELETE CASCADE on patchsets(id). The merge transaction moves
  patchsets_subsystems rows to the target and then runs DELETE FROM
  patchsets for the merged-away row, but never copies
  patchset_maintainer_sections. With foreign keys enabled, the merged-away
  row's sections are deleted without error, so
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns a narrower or empty set, which
  the docs define as closed. Maintainers silently lose transcript access.
  This is the same narrowing the add path's comment says must be avoided.
  Fix: add an INSERT OR IGNORE ... SELECT for the new table next to the
  patchsets_subsystems move, keeping the stronger source on conflict, and
  add a merge test.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections), writes are autocommit
  statements on the single shared libsql connection in Database.conn.
  Database::begin_transaction issues BEGIN IMMEDIATE on that same
  connection with no guard, and src/worker/compressor.rs (compress_messages,
  compress_patches, compress_patchsets) holds it open across awaited work
  and issues ROLLBACK on per-row errors. A section write from another task
  in that window joins the open transaction and is discarded by the
  ROLLBACK while the caller still gets Ok(()). The patchset then authorizes
  nobody and the empty result is read as legitimately closed, with no error
  anywhere. The exposure to the shared connection exists already for other
  writers, but this commit adds authority-bearing writers to it. The bug
  side avoids it by writing through a libsql Transaction. The hazard is
  live if the future ingestion and backfill callers share the compressor's
  Arc<Database>, which is the existing pattern; this commit has no such
  caller, so that is an assumption. Tests use a single task and cannot
  catch it. Fix: serialize writers or give the compressor its own
  connection.

- [LOW] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  the multi-row loop in add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the snapshot
  SELECT, per-row DELETEs and per-row upserts run as separate autocommit
  statements. An error midway (busy timeout, I/O error, kill) leaves a
  half-pruned or partially written set and the caller sees Err with no
  rollback. A concurrent add between the SELECT and the DELETE loop can
  have its row deleted because it is not in the wanted set. The bug-side
  counterpart, update_bug_subsystems, wraps the same work in a transaction.
  The failures are closed and no caller exists yet. Fix: run the body in a
  transaction, subject to the shared-connection caveat above.

- [LOW] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql, the table
  mirrors bug_subsystems but omits the audit triggers from 002_bugs.sql
  (trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source),
  which record reattribution because it decides who can reach the bug.
  Changing a row's source via UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, for example
  path_prefix to maintainers_section, which starts conferring authority,
  and deleting rows in replace_patchset_maintainer_sections leave no
  trace. The bug-side sink, bug_enrichments, is keyed by bug_id and has no
  patchset counterpart, so the triggers cannot be copied verbatim, and no
  design note says the omission is deliberate. Nothing reads the rows yet.
  Fix: add a patchset audit log table and triggers, or document the
  omission as intentional.

Calibration: the failure is closed (access is lost, not widened), the change is recoverable by re-ingesting, and nothing reads the rows yet, so the effect is latent. That makes it Medium. Fix: on the add path keep the stronger source, for example CASE WHEN excluded.source = 'maintainers_section' THEN excluded.source ELSE source END, and add a test that adds the same name with a conflicting source.

findings.problem: patchset section writes join the compressor's open transaction
findings.explanation: Consequence: a section write can return Ok(()) and then be silently undone by another task's ROLLBACK. The patchset then authorizes nobody, and authorizing_sections_for_patchset reports that as a legitimate empty result, so a transcript is closed to its maintainers with no error. It is not Critical or High because the damage fails closed (access is denied rather than granted) and the writers have no non-test caller yet; the commit says 'Nothing reads these rows yet'. Reachability: Database holds one libsql::Connection in `pub conn`. with_bug_actor and with_bug_claim clone that connection, so every handle shares it, and Arc<Database> is held by the ingestor, reviewer, workers and compressor. Database::begin_transaction issues 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE' on self.conn and holds no mutex or guard. The compressor's compress_messages, compress_patches and compress_patchsets each then await spawn-free DB work in a loop before commit_transaction, or run `db.conn.execute("ROLLBACK", ())` on any per-row error. Any statement another task issues on the same connection in that window runs inside the open transaction. add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections both issue autocommit statements on self.conn, so their rows are discarded by that ROLLBACK. Conversely, an existing writer that calls self.conn.transaction() during the window errors with a nested-transaction failure. Other writers already share the connection the same way, so the exposure is pre-existing in the pattern; this commit adds new authority-bearing writers to it. The bug side avoids the problem by writing through a libsql::Transaction (begin_bug_write, with_connection((*tx).clone())); the new functions do not. Same-path defect: replace_patchset_maintainer_sections runs its DELETEs and UPSERTs as separate autocommit statements. An error or crash midway leaves a partially pruned set, again failing closed. Wrapping the whole function in self.conn.transaction() would fix this, but that does not help if the transaction is on the shared connection already in use, so the real fix is to serialize writers or give the compressor its own connection. Assumption: the future ingestion and backfill callers are not in this commit. If they run on the same Arc<Database> as the compressor, which is the existing pattern, the hazard is live. If they use a dedicated connection, it is not. Tests cannot catch this because every test uses a single task and never opens a competing transaction.

findings.problem: patchset section provenance changes and deletes are unaudited
findings.explanation: Consequence and reachability: once a reader consumes these rows, a change to which MAINTAINERS sections a patchset carries, or to a row's source, leaves no trace. Today nothing reads the rows (the commit says so) and no ingestion caller is wired yet, so nothing is exposed yet and the gap is hygiene, hence Low. Verification: 002_bugs.sql defines trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert (AFTER INSERT ON bug_subsystems) and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source (AFTER UPDATE OF source ... WHEN old.source <> new.source). Its comment says 'Reattributing a subsystem decides whether a maintainer can reach the bug at all, so the change is audited'. Both triggers write into bug_enrichments, which is keyed by bug_id. Migration 009 contains no CREATE TRIGGER (grep count is zero). The commit message says the table mirrors bug_subsystems 'down to the source column', and the same authority argument applies to this table. The only patchset-side tables are patchsets, reviews and patchsets_subsystems, none of which is an audit or enrichment sink, so the triggers cannot be copied verbatim. A docs search for audit or patchset_maintainer_sections found nothing, so no design note says the omission is deliberate. Code paths that would go unrecorded: add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections both use UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, whose DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source silently reattributes a row (for example path_prefix to maintainers_section, which starts conferring authority). The replace function's DELETE also removes rows, and the bug side has no delete audit either. The Windows/Linux behaviour is identical. What would confirm or settle this: a patchset audit log table plus the equivalent triggers, or a note stating the omission is intentional. Not Medium because the rows are unread and the bug-side audit is itself not a hard control.

B.summary:
This change adds a new table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that records
which MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches and where each name
came from. It mirrors bug_subsystems so that only rows matched from
MAINTAINERS can grant authority to read a patchset's raw review
transcripts. Mailing list labels from To:/Cc: headers stay separate,
because anyone can put an address in Cc:.

The change adds migration 9 and four database methods: add sections (a
union, since a series arrives one part at a time), replace sections (for
backfill, pruning stale rows), list the authorizing sections, and list
all sections with provenance for display. Nothing reads these rows yet,
so no existing behaviour changes.

Before:
  A patchset had only patchsets_subsystems (mailing list labels and
  path regexes), which cannot decide who may read it. The schema was at
  version 8, and there was no way to record which MAINTAINERS sections
  a patchset touches.

After:
  The schema is at version 9 with a patchset_maintainer_sections table
  keyed by (patchset_id, subsystem). Each row has a source of
  maintainers_section, path_prefix or caller_supplied, defaulting to
  caller_supplied. Only maintainers_section rows are returned by
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset. A patchset with no such rows
  returns an empty list, which the transcript rules are meant to treat
  as closed. Rows are deleted along with their patchset.

The tests cover union across parts, non-MAINTAINERS sources granting no
authority, empty or blank input, pruning on replace, and isolation
between patchsets.
B.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL and
  Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the additive path reuses an
  upsert ending in DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source. A section stored
  as maintainers_section is silently overwritten when a later part supplies
  the same name as path_prefix or caller_supplied. Then
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset stops returning it and maintainers lose
  transcript access with no error or log. The outcome depends on the order
  in which series parts arrive, and contradicts the doc comment that the
  union only grows. Keep the stronger source on conflict in the add path
  (or use DO NOTHING) and keep the overwrite only for replace.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the read, the deletes and the upserts run as separate autocommit
  statements with no transaction. A failure partway (busy database, I/O
  error, cancellation) leaves stale rows pruned and wanted rows partly
  written, and concurrent readers or a concurrent add can see an
  attribution that is neither the old nor the new one. The bug-side
  equivalent is made atomic by update_bug_subsystems, which opens a
  transaction; this pub method does not, so a future backfill gets the
  non-atomic path. Wrap the rewrite in a transaction.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (patchset merge routine) and
  src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql, the merge copies
  only patchsets_subsystems before running DELETE FROM patchsets. The new
  table has ON DELETE CASCADE and foreign keys are enabled in
  Database::new, so the merged-from patchset's MAINTAINERS sections are
  silently deleted instead of being unioned into the target. The target's
  authority-bearing attribution narrows, which is the failure the
  add_patchset_maintainer_sections doc comment says must not happen. It
  fails closed and nothing writes production rows yet, but it becomes live
  once ingestion calls add. Before the delete, copy the rows into the
  target keeping the stronger source, and add a merge test that fails when
  rows are lost.

- [LOW] In src/db.rs (test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts), the
  duplicate section repeats the identical name and source, so the test
  passes even though add overwrites provenance. No test deletes a patchset
  to check the cascade, and none inserts an invalid source to check the
  CHECK constraint. Reverting the provenance handling would fail no test.
  Add a case where the same name arrives with a weaker source.

- [LOW] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql
  (patchset_maintainer_sections), source changes leave no audit record.
  The bug side has triggers trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and
  trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source in 002_bugs.sql that write to
  bug_enrichments; the new table has only indexes. The upsert in
  UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL can therefore grant or revoke read access
  with no record of who or when once a reader exists. The migration comment
  overstates parity with bug attribution. Nothing reads the rows yet, so
  impact is low. Add an audit sink and triggers before the first reader
  lands, or state that changes are not audited.

- [LOW] In src/db.rs (Database::authorizing_sections_for_patchset) and
  src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql, the table is created
  empty with no backfill and no marker of attribution state. Every
  patchset that predates migration 9 returns Ok(empty), identical to
  'populated, no maintainer matched', which the transcript rules treat as
  closed. A gate wired before a backfill runs would deny every maintainer
  on existing series and look like a correct result. No backfill caller
  exists in this commit. Also, the bug side matches scope titles case
  insensitively (COLLATE NOCASE) while this lookup returns stored titles,
  so the gate must compare the same way or a case difference silently
  denies. Fails closed; add a backfill marker or a distinct not-yet-
  attributed result before the gate lands.

Blast radius is limited: the failure is fail-closed, nothing is exposed, and the data is recoverable by a re-run. The fix is to keep the stronger source on conflict in the add path, or use DO NOTHING there and keep the overwrite only for replace.

findings.explanation: Consequence: the function reads, then issues N deletes, then N upserts as separate autocommit statements on self.conn. An error partway through (SQLITE_BUSY, I/O error, future cancellation) leaves stale rows pruned and the wanted rows only partly written. Concurrent readers of authorizing_sections_for_patchset see the intermediate set, and a concurrent add_patchset_maintainer_sections can interleave between the phases. The effect is an attribution that is neither the old nor the new one, with a stale or missing authorizing row. C.summary:
This change adds a new table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that records
which MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches. It mirrors the existing
bug_subsystems table, including the source column. Only rows whose source
is maintainers_section are meant to confer authority over who may read a
patchset's raw review transcripts. The older patchsets_subsystems table
holds mailing list labels from To:/Cc: headers and path regexes, which
anybody can influence, so it cannot be used for that decision.

The change adds migration 9, an upsert statement, and four Database
methods. One adds sections as a union, for ingestion as each part of a
series arrives. One replaces the set exactly and prunes stale rows, for
backfill. One returns only the authorizing sections. One returns every
section with its provenance, for display. Tests cover union across parts,
authority only from maintainers rows, empty attribution, pruning on
replace, and isolation between patchsets.

Before:
  Patchsets had no record of which MAINTAINERS sections they touch. The
  database schema stopped at version 8.

After:
  The database migrates to version 9 on startup and creates an empty
  patchset_maintainer_sections table with two indexes. No existing
  behaviour or output changes, because nothing reads or populates the
  table yet.
C.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL,
  Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections), the upsert ends in
  ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source. A later write that
  names the same section with a weaker source (path_prefix or
  caller_supplied) silently demotes a stored maintainers_section row,
  although the doc comment says add never narrows the attribution.
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset then returns fewer sections with Ok
  and no log, so legitimate maintainers lose access depending on the
  arrival order of series parts. replace collects into a BTreeMap, so
  duplicate names in one slice also resolve by slice order.
  test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts repeats a name only with
  identical provenance, so no test fails if the downgrade exists. The
  failure is closed and nothing reads these rows yet, so it is latent.
  Keep maintainers_section once present (for example a CASE in DO
  UPDATE), merge duplicates by precedence in replace, and add a
  stronger-then-weaker test.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the read, the DELETEs and the upserts are separate autocommit
  statements on the shared connection with no transaction. An error
  between the delete loop and the upsert loop (SQLITE_BUSY, a libsql
  error, a cancelled future) leaves a partially pruned attribution that
  matches neither the old nor the new set, and a caller that logs and
  continues turns this into silent loss of maintainer access. The
  bug-side equivalent is atomic only because
  Database::update_bug_subsystems opens a transaction and runs replace on
  it via with_connection. The patchset function copies the logic without
  that wrapper, and its comment about libsql refusing to commit with a
  statement in progress describes a transaction that does not exist here.
  A concurrent add between the SELECT and the DELETEs would also have its
  new row deleted from the stale read. Open the transaction inside the
  method as update_bug_subsystems does, or make the method private behind
  a transaction-wrapping entry point.

- [LOW] In src/db.rs (Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the loop
  issues one autocommit upsert per section with no atomic boundary. If
  the Nth upsert fails, the function returns Err with sections 1..N-1
  already committed, leaving an arbitrary prefix of a part's sections
  chosen by input order. Upserts are idempotent and add is a union, so a
  retry converges and the failure is closed, but ingestion is not in this
  change so retry behaviour is unknown.

- [LOW] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql
  (patchset_maintainer_sections), provenance changes leave no audit
  trail. The bug side has trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source in 002_bugs.sql,
  which records any change to source because it decides who can reach the
  bug. Migration 009 claims to mirror bug_subsystems but creates only the
  table and two indexes, so a promotion or demotion of source made through
  UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL (via add or replace) cannot be reconstructed
  later. No patchset audit table exists, so a trigger would need a new
  sink. Nothing reads these rows yet, so no wrong access can occur today,
  but the omission is unacknowledged and the impact grows once a consumer
  lands.

findings.problem: patchset section add can demote maintainers_section provenance
findings.explanation: Consequence: a section stored as maintainers_section silently loses authority if a later write names it with a weaker source. The transcript lookup then returns fewer sections, and the caller sees Ok with no error or log. The failure direction is closed, so it denies legitimate maintainers and grants nobody extra access. Reachability: nothing reads these rows yet, so the effect is latent. It becomes live once ingestion and the transcript rules are wired in, and the outcome then depends on the arrival order of series parts. Proof: UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends in ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source. add_patchset_maintainer_sections passes each section's own source straight through. Its doc comment says it adds without removing and that narrowing is what the add/replace split prevents. The primary key allows one row per name, so the last writer wins. The commit's own replace test uses the bare name 'net' under two provenances, so the collision is plausible. replace_patchset_maintainer_sections collects into a BTreeMap, so a duplicate name within one slice also resolves by slice order. Tests: test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts repeats a name only with identical provenance, and no test writes a stronger source and then a weaker one for the same name. Reverting to a precedence-aware upsert would leave every new test green. Fix: keep maintainers_section once present, for example with a CASE in DO UPDATE, merge duplicates by precedence in replace, and add a test for a stronger source followed by a weaker one. Severity is capped at Medium because the failure is closed and no reader exists yet.

findings.problem: patchset section provenance changes leave no audit trail
findings.explanation:
Consequence and reachability: a row in patchset_maintainer_sections can change from path_prefix or caller_supplied to maintainers_section (or the reverse) with no record of the change. Two paths do this. UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends with ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source, and it is used by add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections. Because authorizing_sections_for_patchset filters on source = 'maintainers_section', that change decides who may read a patchset's raw review transcripts. Nothing reads these rows yet, as the commit message says, so no wrong access can occur today. That is why this is Low and not Medium. The impact grows once a consumer lands.

Verification: 002_bugs.sql holds all 11 CREATE TRIGGER statements in src/migrations. They include trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source, which write to bug_enrichments. The comment on the source trigger says reattributing a subsystem 'decides whether a maintainer can reach the bug at all, so the change is audited'. Migration 009 creates only the table and two indexes, with no triggers. Reachability is real, because the upsert path rewrites source whenever the value differs.

The verification question has two parts. (1) Is there an audit table a trigger could write to? No. The only patchset tables are patchsets and patchsets_subsystems (001_initial.sql), and bug_enrichments is keyed by a foreign key to bugs(id). A trigger would need a new patchset audit table, or a different sink, so this is a missing design element and not a one-line omission. (2) Does the commit or a later patch say the omission is intentional? No. git_log from the target to HEAD returns no later commits, and the commit message says only that the table mirrors bug_subsystems 'down to the source column'. It reads as a schema mirror, and the 009 header comment repeats the claim 'The schema mirrors bug_subsystems deliberately'. Neither mentions auditing, so the omission is unacknowledged. The mirror claim covers columns and the CHECK constraint, and it is accurate for those. What is missing is the history guarantee the bug side keeps for the same column. A silent demotion or promotion by the backfill's replace_patchset_maintainer_sections cannot be reconstructed later. Confirmation that would close this: either a patchset audit sink with an AFTER UPDATE OF source trigger, or a note that provenance changes are intentionally unaudited here.
